pathway.title: KBR, INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The spin-off, not the pre-spin ratios, drives the credit view (Documentary Fact for the facts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). The planned separation of Mission Technology Solutions into Trinzic, Inc. is targeted for January 4, 2027, after the cutoff, and is conditional on Board approval, tax treatment, a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, financing and regulatory approvals [business context, transaction register]. That segment carried USD 3,870 million of USD 5,935 million nine-month revenue and USD 441 million of USD 777 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA [business context, calculations], so what remains is the sustainable technology segment plus corporate costs, with USD 336 million of nine-month adjusted EBITDA on the same definition. Management intends to use cash distributed by the departing segment to reduce KBR's debt, but the amount, the allocation of existing debt, and the fate of guarantors and covenants are Not supplied [business context, gaps]. Credit implication: pre-spin leverage cannot be carried forward, and no post-spin leverage claim is made here.

2. Reported leverage is moderate but flattered by a definition change (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Net debt of USD 2,118 million over trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,015 million is 2.1x, against 2.2x at January 2, 2026, and gross leverage is 2.52x [financial base, leverage chart]. Since the first quarter of fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA adds back joint venture items of USD 44 million over nine months without recasting history; without them net leverage is 2.18x, almost level with 2.19x at the end of fiscal 2025, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization it is 2.37x [financial base, definition review]. Credit implication: most of the apparent improvement is definitional, so covenant judgments should use the lower-quality measures as well.

3. A refinancing and amortization step falls inside twelve months (Documentary Fact). Current maturities of long-term debt are USD 554 million at October 2, 2026 against USD 49 million at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; the USD 250 million Senior Notes mature in September 2028, and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029 [financial base, debt schedule]. Liquidity is USD 1,046 million, made of cash of USD 439 million and USD 607 million undrawn on the revolver after letters of credit, against the USD 625 million revolver capacity stated in the release [financial base, liquidity chart]. Credit implication: the tranche can be repaid from liquidity or refinanced, but its timing coincides with the separation, when lender consent, ratings and covenant terms are being reset (Amendment No. 14 already permitted the reorganization).

4. Covenant headroom cannot be tested (Insufficient Information). The filings describe a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 4.00x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, with compliance stated at every reported date, but the credit agreement, Amendment No. 14 and the indenture are Not supplied and the covenant ratios are not printed [financial base, covenants]. On the company basis the indicative figures are 2.09x net leverage and 7.00x adjusted EBITDA to interest expense. Credit implication: the cushion looks wide on any measure computed here, but it is indicative only, because defined terms and joint venture add-back treatment are unknown (see Calculations).

5. Cash conversion depends on working capital, joint venture distributions and receivable sales (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 331 million against USD 506 million a year earlier, a simple free cash flow build is USD 295 million, equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates was USD 167 million of operating income of USD 538 million (31.0%) against cash distributions of earnings of USD 145 million, and USD 935 million of receivables were sold and settled in the period, leaving USD 65 million outstanding, unchanged from the start of the year [financial base, claims outside debt; business context, calculations]. Cash interest paid is available for fiscal 2025 only, where adjusted EBITDA covered it 6.87x. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate on the evidence but rests on cash that KBR does not fully control, and the interim cash cover is Not supplied.

6. Customer concentration and budget timing shape revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the U.K. government 9%; backlog was USD 17,718 million, 38% executable within one year, USD 9.0 billion of the departing segment's backlog is funded, nearly all contracts can be terminated for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the U.S. government only to December 11, 2026 [business context, operating model]. Credit implication: revenue is visible but not contractual, and the concentration moves with the segment that is leaving, so the remaining group's profile is more commercial and more tied to energy and chemicals project cycles, which the evidence describes only in part.

7. Behaviour to date is not creditor-adverse on documented actions (Analyst Interpretation). Buybacks fell to USD 29 million over nine months from USD 304 million, the dividend was kept at USD 63 million, acquisitions were small in fiscal 2025, and no priming, uptier or leakage is documented; USD 177 million of minority and joint venture investments were made in nine months (USD 115 million in one joint venture, USD 49 million in securities and USD 13 million in other investments) [business context, governance]. Credit implication: discretionary cash returns are a lever management has used to conserve cash, but legal capacity under the credit agreement is untested and a post-spin capital allocation policy is Not supplied.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity is a clear strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,046 million of cash and undrawn revolver, against a first scheduled tranche of USD 554 million and no maturity of the Senior Notes until September 2028 [financial base]. Leverage is moderate on every measure computed, from 2.1x as printed to 2.37x unadjusted, well below the described 4.00x covenant ceiling (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only). Revenue visibility from a backlog of USD 17,718 million, with USD 9.0 billion of the Mission Technology Solutions backlog funded and USD 5,404 million of award options (Documentary Fact) [business context]. Diversified end markets and geography beyond the U.S. government, with commercial and infrastructure clients and international government clients contributing USD 2,454 million and USD 905 million in fiscal 2025 (Documentary Fact). Cash returns are discretionary and have been reduced, with USD 402 million of repurchase authorization remaining, which gives management a lever in a stress (Analyst Interpretation). The management description of a low capital intensity model with favorable operating cash flows is Management Language and is not adopted; the financial base shows nine-month capital expenditure of USD 36 million against operating cash flow of USD 331 million, which is consistent with it.

Weaknesses. The post-spin capital structure is Not supplied (Insufficient Information): the debt allocation, the Senior Notes guarantor perimeter and covenants after separation determine the credit, and missing evidence is not treated as adverse. Adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026 and mixes two bases in its trailing figure (Documentary Fact). Near-term amortization and the August 2027 tranche arrive during the separation (Documentary Fact). Earnings include a large share of equity-method income (USD 167 million of USD 538 million of operating income) whose cash arrives only as distributions (Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is concentrated in one sovereign customer in the segment that leaves, and fiscal budgets run on continuing resolutions (Documentary Fact). Nine-month operating cash flow declined by USD 175 million to USD 331 million (Documentary Fact, from USD 506 million). Contingent items outside the debt figure include an unaccrued USD 41 million Kuwait court judgment under appeal and letters of credit of USD 18 million on the revolver and USD 305 million on bilateral lines (Documentary Fact). Interim cash interest is Not supplied and covenant definitions are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).

runs.text: The one transaction in the pack is the Planned Spin-Off of the Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into Trinzic, Inc., announced in September 2025 and targeted for January 4, 2027, after the evidence cutoff. It is a spin-off to shareholders, not a sale, merger or sponsor transaction, so there is no purchase price, sponsor equity or acquisition financing. It is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing and regulatory approvals. For creditors, the mechanism is that MTS makes a cash distribution to KBR from its own financing before completion, which management intends to use to reduce KBR's debt; the amount, the debt that stays with each company and the treatment of guarantors, liens and covenants are not supplied. Spin-off costs and other charges were 24 in the third quarter and 70 over nine months fiscal 2026. No new notes, term loan or other debt issue by KBR, INC. appears in the periods covered: the financing events are revolver borrowings of 281 and repayments of 301, scheduled repayments of 29 on Term Loan A and 8 on Term Loan B, and Amendment No. 14 to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026, which permits internal reorganization transactions for the spin-off and makes other modifications that are not described. Management states that the spin-off is tax-free in intent, and that KBR and Trinzic expect to launch as independent companies in January, which is Management Language. Liquidity effects, debt maturities and covenant levels are in the financial base module. The earlier timing statement of the second half of fiscal 2026 was superseded by the January 4, 2027 target from the first quarter of fiscal 2026 onward, and is logged as a conflict below. Trinzic's own financing terms are Not supplied.

fields.value: KBR enters the cut-off with a moderately levered balance sheet, drifting toward lower reported leverage, and a perimeter about to change. On management's own measure, net debt of 2,118 against trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA of 1,015 gives 2.1x at October 2, 2026, compared with 2.2x at January 2, 2026, 2.3x at April 3, 2026 and 2.3x at July 3, 2026. Gross debt principal was 2,557 at October 2, 2026, made up of 957 Term Loan A, 975 Term Loan B, 250 of 4.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and 375 drawn on the 1,000 revolver. On the same earnings measure gross leverage is 2.52x and net leverage is 2.09x. Those ratios carry a definition risk that matters for the credit view. Beginning with the first quarter of fiscal 2026, adjusted EBITDA was revised to add back the group's share of joint venture interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization and acquisition costs, prospectively and without recasting history; the add-back is 44 over nine months of fiscal 2026. Removing it gives trailing EBITDA of 971 and net leverage of 2.18x, which is almost level with the 2.19x computed for fiscal 2025, so nearly all of the reported improvement reflects the change of definition. The measure also adds back spin-off, acquisition and restructuring costs of 72 over nine months (18 a year earlier), and starts from operating income that includes equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates of 167 against cash distributions of earnings of 145. A plain operating income plus depreciation and amortization proxy for the trailing twelve months is 895, which gives net leverage of 2.37x on this unadjusted basis.

fields.value: Cover is available on cash interest only for fiscal 2025: adjusted EBITDA of 968 over cash interest paid of 141 gives 6.87x. No 2026 cash interest figure is supplied in the interim sources, so the interim cover cells are Not supplied. As a labelled memo, adjusted EBITDA over interest expense is 7.00x on a trailing basis to October 2, 2026 (interest expense of 145). Liquidity at October 2, 2026 is cash of 439 plus 607 undrawn on the committed revolver after 18 of letters of credit, 1,046 in total. The release states revolver capacity of 625, which is the commitment less borrowings with no deduction for the letters of credit; the 10-Q reports the letters separately. Bilateral and uncommitted lines of 491 can be used for letters of credit only, with 186 unused, and are excluded from liquidity. Of the 439 cash, 67 is joint venture and Aspire Defence project cash and the captive insurer holds part of the domestic balance, so the cash that is freely available is smaller than the headline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first scheduled wall is near. Current maturities of long-term debt are 554 at October 2, 2026, against 49 at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; Senior Notes follow in September 2028 and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029. The refinancing sits alongside the planned spin-off targeted for January 4, 2027, after which management intends to use cash distributed by the MTS business to reduce debt; the amount, the post-spin debt and the post-spin earnings are not supplied. For scale, MTS carried 441 of nine-month adjusted EBITDA out of 777, and the other segment plus corporate carried 336. Operating cash flow of 331 for nine months fiscal 2026 compares with 506 a year earlier. Receivable monetization programs sold 935 in the period and settled 935, leaving 65 outstanding, the same as at the start of the year, so the programs did not add net funding over nine months but remain a recurring working capital tool. Claims outside the debt figure include operating and finance leases, a 41 Kuwait court judgment under appeal that is not accrued, letters of credit and surety support, and a United Kingdom pension surplus rather than a deficit. The view is therefore moderate leverage, adequate liquidity, a near-term amortization step, an EBITDA definition that flatters the trend, and a covenant package that cannot be tested against defined terms.

fields.value: The Senior Credit Facility has two maintenance tests as the filings describe them: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "may not exceed 4.25 to 1 in 2023, reducing to 4.00 to 1 in 2024 and thereafter" for consolidated net leverage and [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "may not be less than 3.00 to 1 as of the last day of any fiscal quarter" for consolidated interest coverage. Compliance is stated for every reported date, most recently [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "As of October 2, 2026, we were in compliance with our financial covenants under our Senior Credit Facility." The reported covenant ratio is not printed. On the company basis computed here, net leverage of 2.09x sits below the described 4.00x ceiling and interest expense cover of 7.00x sits above the 3.00x floor; both are indicative only because the defined terms, any amendment effect from Amendment No. 14 and the treatment of joint venture add-backs are not available. The margin grid on the revolver and Term Loan A steps at net leverage of 4.25x, 3.25x, 2.25x and 1.25x, so the indicative 2.09x level would place pricing in the band below 2.25x, subject to the defined ratio.

The business has two core segments. Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) serves defense, intelligence, space and civil government customers, mainly in the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia, largely on cost-reimbursable terms; U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and U.K. government customers 9%. Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) licenses proprietary process technology and provides engineering and advisory services to energy and chemicals customers, with a large equity-method joint venture component. The operating model is capital light, project and program based, and dependent on backlog conversion, working capital and joint venture distributions; backlog was 17,718 at October 2, 2026, plus 5,404 of award options, of which 38% is expected to be executed within one year, and nearly all contracts allow termination for convenience.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction that dominates the credit view is the Planned Spin-Off of MTS into a separate listed company, to be named Trinzic, Inc., first announced in September 2025 and now targeted for January 4, 2027, the first business day of fiscal 2027, after the evidence cutoff. Completion is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing, and regulatory approvals. The mechanism that matters to creditors is that MTS is the larger segment by revenue, adjusted EBITDA and backlog, so after separation the remaining KBR group is the STS business plus corporate costs, while management says it will use cash distributed by MTS from its own financing to reduce KBR's debt. The size of that distribution, which debt stays with which company, whether the Senior Credit Facility and the Senior Notes remain with KBR, and the covenant and guarantor perimeter after separation are not supplied. The July 29, 2026 Amendment No. 14 to the credit agreement permits the internal reorganization; its text is not supplied. Behaviour to date is that of a company preparing a separation while keeping its dividend, cutting buybacks, and making small acquisitions and minority investments, with no documented priming, non-pro-rata exchange or distribution to insiders. The creditor view is therefore: a business with diversified government and commercial exposure, moderate leverage and large pending structural change, where the post-spin perimeter, debt allocation and covenant package, not the pre-spin credit statistics, will decide the credit quality, and where those facts are not yet in the pack.

It is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing and regulatory approvals. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: KBR, INC. is a moderately levered, well-funded defense and sustainable-technology services group whose credit is sound on today's numbers but is about to be reset by the planned spin-off of its larger segment. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,046 million, net leverage of 2.1x on management's measure and a backlog of USD 17,718 million. The weakest point is that adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026, current maturities rose to USD 554 million, and no post-spin debt, covenant or guarantor terms are disclosed. The outcome turns on how much debt the Mission Technology Solutions cash distribution retires, how the August 2027 term loan is refinanced, and whether the remaining sustainable technology group can carry the capital structure it inherits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium, held below High because the covenant, indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, the post-spin capital structure is Not supplied, and the business context was ready only with limitations. Basis: financial base leverage, liquidity, maturity and definition rows; business context transaction, customer concentration, backlog and governance rows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis: KBR, INC. can service and refinance its present debt from liquidity and recurring government and technology programs, but its credit quality will be decided by the debt, covenants and earnings base it carries after the Mission Technology Solutions spin-off, which the evidence does not yet show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The spin-off, not the pre-spin ratios, drives the credit view (Documentary Fact for the facts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). The planned separation of Mission Technology Solutions into Trinzic, Inc. is targeted for January 4, 2027, after the cutoff, and is conditional on Board approval, tax treatment, a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, financing and regulatory approvals [business context, transaction register]. That segment carried USD 3,870 million of USD 5,935 million nine-month revenue and USD 441 million of USD 777 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA [business context, calculations], so what remains is the sustainable technology segment plus corporate costs, with USD 336 million of nine-month adjusted EBITDA on the same definition. Management intends to use cash distributed by the departing segment to reduce KBR's debt, but the amount, the allocation of existing debt, and the fate of guarantors and covenants are Not supplied [business context, gaps]. Credit implication: pre-spin leverage cannot be carried forward, and no post-spin leverage claim is made here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Reported leverage is moderate but flattered by a definition change (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Net debt of USD 2,118 million over trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,015 million is 2.1x, against 2.2x at January 2, 2026, and gross leverage is 2.52x [financial base, leverage chart]. Since the first quarter of fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA adds back joint venture items of USD 44 million over nine months without recasting history; without them net leverage is 2.18x, almost level with 2.19x at the end of fiscal 2025, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization it is 2.37x [financial base, definition review]. Credit implication: most of the apparent improvement is definitional, so covenant judgments should use the lower-quality measures as well.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. A refinancing and amortization step falls inside twelve months (Documentary Fact). Current maturities of long-term debt are USD 554 million at October 2, 2026 against USD 49 million at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; the USD 250 million Senior Notes mature in September 2028, and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029 [financial base, debt schedule]. Liquidity is USD 1,046 million, made of cash of USD 439 million and USD 607 million undrawn on the revolver after letters of credit, against the USD 625 million revolver capacity stated in the release [financial base, liquidity chart]. Credit implication: the tranche can be repaid from liquidity or refinanced, but its timing coincides with the separation, when lender consent, ratings and covenant terms are being reset (Amendment No. 14 already permitted the reorganization).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Covenant headroom cannot be tested (Insufficient Information). The filings describe a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 4.00x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, with compliance stated at every reported date, but the credit agreement, Amendment No. 14 and the indenture are Not supplied and the covenant ratios are not printed [financial base, covenants]. On the company basis the indicative figures are 2.09x net leverage and 7.00x adjusted EBITDA to interest expense. Credit implication: the cushion looks wide on any measure computed here, but it is indicative only, because defined terms and joint venture add-back treatment are unknown (see Calculations).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Cash conversion depends on working capital, joint venture distributions and receivable sales (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 331 million against USD 506 million a year earlier, a simple free cash flow build is USD 295 million, equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates was USD 167 million of operating income of USD 538 million (31.0%) against cash distributions of earnings of USD 145 million, and USD 935 million of receivables were sold and settled in the period, leaving USD 65 million outstanding, unchanged from the start of the year [financial base, claims outside debt; business context, calculations]. Cash interest paid is available for fiscal 2025 only, where adjusted EBITDA covered it 6.87x. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate on the evidence but rests on cash that KBR does not fully control, and the interim cash cover is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Customer concentration and budget timing shape revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the U.K. government 9%; backlog was USD 17,718 million, 38% executable within one year, USD 9.0 billion of the departing segment's backlog is funded, nearly all contracts can be terminated for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the U.S. government only to December 11, 2026 [business context, operating model]. Credit implication: revenue is visible but not contractual, and the concentration moves with the segment that is leaving, so the remaining group's profile is more commercial and more tied to energy and chemicals project cycles, which the evidence describes only in part.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Behaviour to date is not creditor-adverse on documented actions (Analyst Interpretation). Buybacks fell to USD 29 million over nine months from USD 304 million, the dividend was kept at USD 63 million, acquisitions were small in fiscal 2025, and no priming, uptier or leakage is documented; USD 177 million of minority and joint venture investments were made in nine months (USD 115 million in one joint venture, USD 49 million in securities and USD 13 million in other investments) [business context, governance]. Credit implication: discretionary cash returns are a lever management has used to conserve cash, but legal capacity under the credit agreement is untested and a post-spin capital allocation policy is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity is a clear strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,046 million of cash and undrawn revolver, against a first scheduled tranche of USD 554 million and no maturity of the Senior Notes until September 2028 [financial base]. Leverage is moderate on every measure computed, from 2.1x as printed to 2.37x unadjusted, well below the described 4.00x covenant ceiling (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only). Revenue visibility from a backlog of USD 17,718 million, with USD 9.0 billion of the Mission Technology Solutions backlog funded and USD 5,404 million of award options (Documentary Fact) [business context]. Diversified end markets and geography beyond the U.S. government, with commercial and infrastructure clients and international government clients contributing USD 2,454 million and USD 905 million in fiscal 2025 (Documentary Fact). Cash returns are discretionary and have been reduced, with USD 402 million of repurchase authorization remaining, which gives management a lever in a stress (Analyst Interpretation). The management description of a low capital intensity model with favorable operating cash flows is Management Language and is not adopted; the financial base shows nine-month capital expenditure of USD 36 million against operating cash flow of USD 331 million, which is consistent with it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. The post-spin capital structure is Not supplied (Insufficient Information): the debt allocation, the Senior Notes guarantor perimeter and covenants after separation determine the credit, and missing evidence is not treated as adverse. Adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026 and mixes two bases in its trailing figure (Documentary Fact). Near-term amortization and the August 2027 tranche arrive during the separation (Documentary Fact). Earnings include a large share of equity-method income (USD 167 million of USD 538 million of operating income) whose cash arrives only as distributions (Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is concentrated in one sovereign customer in the segment that leaves, and fiscal budgets run on continuing resolutions (Documentary Fact). Nine-month operating cash flow declined by USD 175 million to USD 331 million (Documentary Fact, from USD 506 million). Contingent items outside the debt figure include an unaccrued USD 41 million Kuwait court judgment under appeal and letters of credit of USD 18 million on the revolver and USD 305 million on bilateral lines (Documentary Fact). Interim cash interest is Not supplied and covenant definitions are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).

fields.value: The analysis is traceable enough for restricted committee use. Nearly every figure in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis traces to a located page in the pinned filings, and recomputation from separately extracted filing lines reproduced gross debt, net debt, trailing adjusted EBITDA, liquidity and the maturity schedule. The most important provenance gap is covenant compliance and the post-spin structure: the credit agreement, its Amendment No. 14 and the Form 10 are not in the pack, so statements that covenants are met are management assertions and the surviving credit cannot be sized. A second gap is the cash flow attribution, which the cash flow statement does not support as written. The defects found are minor and none changes the credit view. Because the same analyst wrote the modules and this trace, an independent reviewer should repeat the highest-risk checks before the report is used.
